bottom_line: In patients with NYHA class II heart failure and an ejection fraction of no more than 35%, eplerenone vs placebo reduced the primary outcome of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, eplerenone compared with placebo lowered the risk of the composite of cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization (HR 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74) and reduced all-cause death (HR 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.93), while increasing the proportion with serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L (11.8% vs 7.2%). The results may not extend to patients who would not have met the trial’s eligibility criteria or safety exclusions.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in 2737 patients with NYHA class II heart failure and LVEF ≤35% receiving recommended therapy.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 2737 patients with New York Heart Association class II heart failure and an ejection fraction of no more than 35% to receive eplerenone (up to 50 mg daily) or placebo

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death or first hospitalization for heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes or a first hospital- ization for heart failure.

major_points.text: Trial stopped early after the prespecified stopping boundary for overwhelming benefit was crossed; median follow-up 21 months.
major_points.quote: The trial was stopped prematurely, according to prespecified rules, after a median follow-up period of 21 months.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred in 18.3% with eplerenone vs 25.9% with placebo (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54–0.74; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 18.3% of patients in the eplerenone group as compared with 25.9% in the placebo group (hazard ra- tio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54 to 0.74; P<0.001).

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was 12.5% with eplerenone vs 15.5% with placebo (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62–0.93; P=0.008).
major_points.quote: A total of 12.5% of patients receiving eplerenone and 15.5% of those receiving placebo died (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.93; P = 0.008)

major_points.text: Hyperkalemia risk increased: serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L occurred in 11.8% with eplerenone vs 7.2% with placebo (P<0.001).
major_points.quote: A serum potassium level above 5.5 mmol per liter was reported in 158 of 1336 patients (11.8%) in the eplerenone group and 96 of 1340 patients (7.2%) in the placebo group (P<0.001).

Eligibility criteria were as follows: an age of at least 55 years, NYHA functional class II symp- toms

inclusion_criteria.text: Ejection fraction no more than 30% (or if >30 to 35%, QRS duration >130 msec).
inclusion_criteria.quote: an ejection fraction of no more than 30% (or, if >30 to 35%, a QRS duration of >130 msec on electrocardiography)

inclusion_criteria.text: Treatment with ACE inhibitor, ARB, or both and a beta-blocker (unless contraindicated) at recommended or maximal tolerated dose.
inclusion_criteria.quote: and treatment with an angiotensin-converting–enzyme (ACE) inhibitor, an angiotensin-receptor blocker (ARB), or both and a beta-blocker (unless contraindicated) at the recommended dose or maximal tolerated dose.

inclusion_criteria.text: Randomization within 6 months after hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Randomization was to occur within 6 months after hospitalization for a cardiovascular reason.

inclusion_criteria.text: If not hospitalized within 6 months: BNP ≥250 pg/mL or NT-proBNP ≥500 pg/mL in men and ≥750 pg/mL in women.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who had not been hospitalized for a car- diovascular reason within 6 months before the screening visit could be enrolled if the plasma level of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) was at least 250 pg per milliliter
